text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Denmark's second largest airport Billund in Jutland continues to grow with 1.6 million passengers in the first ten months of 1996, a 15.7 percent increase over last year. About a quarter of the passengers used the airport for foreign flights, a 27.8 percent rise.

--- Danish State Oil and Natural Gas (DONG) is threatening to withdraw from a major oil project in Lithuania if the Vilnius government does not change tax legislation demanding 20 percent for research and 29 percent for use of oil deposits. DONG has spent six million crowns on the project.

--- Tele Danmark Cable TV and rival cable company Stofa now plan to give parents the possibility of controlling their childrens' television viewing by introducing a special system to control access to certain channels.
--- The ongoing air flight price war has forced Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) to cut fares to Madrid, Barcelona, Rome, Milan, Nice and Vienna to 1,900 Danish crowns return until the New Year.

--- Danish companies should not expect a lowering of corporate taxes to 26 percent from the present 34 percent rate after the breakdown of the 1997 state budget negotiations between the minority Social Democratic-led government and the opposition Conservatives last Friday, government sources say.
